items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: 'Course, Ray Charles, Bobby Blue Bland, B.B. King an' all them fellows, they were doin' the same thing.

ctx.x: We run into a lot of people down there used to book dances. So's we worked for them all through Texas. I was down in Texas so much until I lived down there. So when I leave Texas, I'd go home. I lived in Chicago. I moved up in Chicago where I met a lady. Her name was Louella Brown. I wrote a song about her--Louella Brown. So I met her in Chicago, and I...we got married. I lived with her seventeen years. She used to travel on the road with me, and we had a ball. We bought several homes in Chicago. I had coupla…

Then, every summer we take off and go down through Texas and Louisiana, Mississippi, Tennessee. We play all over the South. I don't think there's a place in the South where I ain't never been. I made so many stops...one-nighters...call me "One-Nighters Joe." 'Course, Ray Charles, Bobby Blue Bland, B.B. King an' all them fellows, they were doin' the same thing. That's all we played was one-nighters. We didn't play too many nightclubs. When we did, we just stayed three days... weekends...and we had a lot of fun…

So we talkin' about whenever anybody would have a good night ...made some extra money...we'd all come out and have a good time the next day. I had a friend of mine called Herman the German. I met him down in Houston, Texas. I was workin' at a place called the Peacock Nightclub. Don Roby (?) run it, and, uh...we, uh, used to play there sometimes a month in the nightclub, and so I run into Herman the German
